intro: In the mixed drill the idioms of the 気, body-part and four-character sets compete. Do not translate word by word. First decide what kind of thing the sentence describes (a feeling, a person, an action towards others, or a verdict on how things turned out), then take the expression from that family, and finally check that it fits the frame around the blank.

skills.rule: Feeling: 気, 腹 or 頭. Trait of a person: body part or 気 + adjective. Action towards others: 手, 足, 肩 or 気を + verb. Verdict on the outcome: a four-character idiom with だ.
skills.explain:
Ask in order.

1. Is it a feeling in the moment? Anger is 腹が立つ (blunter: 頭に来る). Something nagging at you is 気になる; dread of something ahead is 気が重い; relief is 気が楽になる.

2. Is it a lasting trait of a person? A body part or 気 with an adjective: knows many people 顔が広い, keeps secrets 口が堅い, skilled 腕がいい, impatient 気が短い, thoughtful 気が利く.

3. Is it something one person does to or for others? 手, 足 or 肩 with a verb: help 手を貸す, hold back 足を引っ張る, take sides 肩を持つ, be considerate 気を遣う.

4. Is it a comment summing up how things turned out? A four-character idiom with だ: two gains 一石二鳥, deserved trouble 自業自得, quitting early 三日坊主.

5. Check the frame: the particles around the blank stay as they are (物音が気になる, 態度に腹が立つ), and four-character idioms take だ, で or する.
patterns: feeling: [cause] に 腹が立つ / [thing] が 気になる
trait: [person] は 顔が広い / 口が堅い / 腕がいい
action: [person] に 手を貸す / の 足を引っ張る / の 肩を持つ
verdict: [situation] は 一石二鳥だ / 自業自得だ

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]の失礼[しつれい]な態度[たいど]に{腹[はら]が立[た]った}。
examples.en: My little brother's rude attitude made me angry.

examples.jp: 隣[となり]の部屋[へや]の物音[ものおと]が{気[き]になって}、眠[ねむ]れない。
examples.en: The noises from the next room keep bothering me and I can't sleep.

examples.jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの日[ひ]、友達[ともだち]が{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれた。
examples.en: On moving day my friends gave me a hand.

examples.jp: 山本[やまもと]さんは{口[くち]が堅[かた]い}から、相談[そうだん]しても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だ。
examples.en: Yamamoto-san can keep a secret, so it's safe to ask her advice.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]まで歩[ある]けば運動[うんどう]になるし、バス代[だい]も浮[う]くから{一石二鳥[いっせきにちょう]}だ。
examples.en: Walking to the station gives me exercise and saves the bus fare, so it's two birds with one stone.

examples.jp: 毎晩[まいばん]夜更[よふ]かしして風邪[かぜ]をひいたのは{自業自得[じごうじとく]}だ。
examples.en: Catching a cold after staying up late every night is my own fault.

contrast.vs: 腹が立つ ↔ 気になる
contrast.note: 腹が立つ is anger at something (に). 気になる is being bothered or curious, without anger (が). 態度に腹が立つ versus 物音が気になる.

contrast.vs: 手を貸す ↔ 肩を持つ
contrast.note: Both are on someone's side. 手を貸す is practical help with a task; 肩を持つ is siding with someone in an argument.

contrast.vs: 一石二鳥 ↔ 自業自得
contrast.note: Both sum up a result. Two gains from one act: 一石二鳥. A bad result someone caused themselves: 自業自得.

mistakes.bad: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの日[ひ]、友達[ともだち]が{肩[かた]を持[も]って}くれた。
mistakes.good: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの日[ひ]、友達[ともだち]が{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれた。
mistakes.note: Help with a task is 手を貸す. 肩を持つ means taking someone's side in a dispute, not carrying things.

mistakes.bad: 隣[となり]の部屋[へや]の物音[ものおと]に{気[き]がついて}、眠[ねむ]れない。
mistakes.good: 隣[となり]の部屋[へや]の物音[ものおと]が{気[き]になって}、眠[ねむ]れない。
mistakes.note: Noticing once does not keep you awake; a noise that keeps bothering you is 気になる.

mistakes.bad: 田中[たなか]さんは{顔[かお]が広[ひろ]い}から、秘密[ひみつ]を話[はな]しても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だ。
mistakes.good: 田中[たなか]さんは{口[くち]が堅[かた]い}から、秘密[ひみつ]を話[はな]しても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だ。
mistakes.note: Safe with a secret is 口が堅い. 顔が広い means knowing many people, which is no reason to trust them with one.

skills.tip: Label the blank first: feeling, trait, action or verdict. That alone removes most of the options.
